body: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly act as personal assistants; however, little is known about how they capture national-level preferences on a global scale. Given that "time" is a universal and representative concept, we examine LLMs' time preferences by varying only users' country and measuring the compensation LLMs deem appropriate for a 60-minute appointment delay. We then compare LLMs' responses with GDP per capita on Purchasing Power Parity (GDP_PPP), Mean Income, and a literature-based index (Patience Score). Our results across 193 countries and 5 LLMs demonstrate that people's time across the world is evaluated in noticeably different ways among LLMs, as well as varying levels of robustness under prompt variations. LLMs consistently recommend the highest compensation for Europe, but mostly the lowest for Africa. Based on GDP_PPP, LLMs underestimate the value of time for users living in Asia and South America. These findings indicate that geographical patterns are embedded in LLMs and may translate in different treatment in agentic settings.
summaryZh: 本文通过测量大模型对不同国家用户时间价值的评估，探讨了模型中嵌入的全球性偏见。研究发现，LLM在处理不同国家用户的补偿建议时存在显著差异，且与GDP等经济指标存在不一致性。这种地理模式的差异表明模型在智能体应用中可能产生不公平的对待，为理解大模型的社会影响提供了实证视角。
